core_obligations: Identify the Cech complex with a Hom complex: use that the Cech complex of U with coefficients in I is obtained by applying Hom_{PAb(C)}(-, I) to Z^bullet_U, so that H^p-check(U, I) = H^p(Hom_{PAb(C)}(Z^bullet_U, I)) (proof lines 1709-1716).
Transfer exactness: Z^bullet_U is exact in negative degrees and Hom_{PAb(C)}(-, I) is exact because I is injective in PAb(C), so the Hom complex is exact in positive degrees (proof lines 1717-1720).
Conclude the vanishing: the cohomology of that complex in positive degrees is zero, which is exactly H^p-check(U, I) = 0 for all p > 0 (statement line 1705, proof lines 1719-1720).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite Cech cohomology as the cohomology of the Hom complex out of Z^bullet_U (proof lines 1709-1716).
Use exactness of Z^bullet_U in negative degrees plus exactness of the Hom functor into an injective to get exactness of the Hom complex in positive degrees (proof lines 1717-1720).
Read off the vanishing of all positive Cech cohomology groups (proof line 1720).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the acyclicity input for the Cech-to-derived comparison: if I is an injective object of the category of abelian presheaves on the site, then its Cech cohomology with respect to any family vanishes in positive degrees (statement lines 1703-1705). The proof works by a degree shift: the Cech complex is the Hom complex out of Z^bullet_U, and since Z^bullet_U is exact in negative degrees, the exactness of Hom(-, I) for injective I produces exactness in positive degrees rather than in negative ones (proof lines 1709-1720). Guessing that shift, and that it is the reason the statement is about positive degrees, is the non-formal part. The claim is H2: four lines, one functor, one shift.
